document.title: Isotopic constraints on atmospheric sulfate formation pathways in the Mt. Everest region, southern Tibetan Plateau
warnings: No 'Abstract' heading detected; treated the front matter as the abstract.

tldr.text: In this study, we report observations of sulfate concentrations and 117O(SO2− 4 ) in aerosol samples collected from the Mt.

Intriguingly, a seasonal variation of 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS with high values during the monsoon (warm) season and low values in the pre-monsoon (cold) season was observed in this study, which is opposite to that of 117O(NO− 3 ) measured from the same aerosol samples as well as that of 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS observed from the polar regions.

problem.text: This high 117O in non-dust sulfate found in this region clearly indicates the important role of the S(IV)+O3 pathway in atmospheric sulfate formation promoted by conditions of high cloud water pH.

Overall, our study provides an observational constraint on atmospheric acidity in altering sulfate formation pathways, particularly in dust-rich environments, and such identification of key processes provides an important basis for a better understanding of the sulfur cycle in the TP.

approach.text: With these expectations, here, for the first time, we present relatively long term 117O observations in atmospheric sulfate as well as its concentrations in this region, which is also an important addition to the global sulfate isotope dataset.

results.text: The results show that, if the cloud water pH is fixed to 4.5, the modeled monthlymean 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS values range from 0.5 ‰ to 0.7 ‰ during the sampling period (April to September), significantly lower than the observed monthly weighted average 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS values with a range of 1.0 ‰ to 2.1 ‰ in the Mt.
The above results show that the consideration of variable cloud water pH significantly improved the model’s ability to simulate the 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS in the Mt.

Everest region would facilitate the heterogeneous SO2 oxidation by O3 on the alkaline dust surface, which increases the overall fraction of the S(IV) + O3 reaction and results in relatively higher 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS values in the monsoon season than that in the pre-monsoon season.

evidence.quote: Everest region, in turn, highlights observational evidence that atmospheric acidity plays an important role in controlling sulfate formation pathways, particularly for dust-rich environments.
Consequently, our findings provide an important observational basis for better constraints on the importance of pH in sulfate formation pathways.

Consequently, an accurate estimate of cloud water pH in the model simulation and elucidation of its relation to atmospheric sulfate formation are necessary for precise model forecasts, and observations of 117O(SO2− 4 )SAS are important constraints on model validation.
